Target rider: Expert freeriders who like to crush steep terrain at top speed [32] 107. Ideal conditions: Deep powder, steep terrain, firm groomers, variable conditions [38] 108. Riding style: High-speed freeriding, big mountain descents, freeride competitions [25] 109. Not recommended for: Beginners, park/jib riders, riders seeking playful/forgiving boards, mellow cruising [39] 110. Not recommended for: Tight tree riding at slow speeds [40] 111. All mountain rating: 9/10 [1] 112. Powder rating: 10/10 [1] 113. Freestyle rating: 5/10 [1] 114. High-speed stability: Exceptional — "feels confident at any speed, eats up chatter like it's nothing" [18] 115. Edge hold: Strong — Traction Tech locks in; "feels locked in the moment you set an edge" on firm groomers [41] 116. Float in powder: Excellent — tapered directional shape, 3D contour base, and setback all contribute to float [42] 117. Pop: More pop than the regular Flagship; "you definitely get more pop out of this" [13] 118. Damping: Very damp — "pretty damp, with more pop and only $150 more than the regular Flagship" [13] 119. Carving: Can hold high-speed carves with ease; allows high-angle carves without washout [42] 120. Buttering ability: Nearly impossible to butter due to stiff flex, but early rise in tips provides some cheater leverage [13] 121. Switch riding: "Very doable switch and very good for hitting big kickers for being so directional" — rocker in tail makes switch landings easier [43] 122. Slow-speed maneuverability: Takes effort to switch edges at slower speeds; "not the quickest edge-to-edge" but manageable [42] 123. Durability (build quality): "Nothing rattles, nothing feels cheap and I never had a weird vibration or delam scare. It feels like a board you buy to keep for years." [41] 127. K2 Alchemist: Listed as similar board to the Jones Flagship by The Good Ride review [50] 140.
